scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You pay the same EMI every month, yet in the first years your loan barely shrinks. Why?

scenes.name: what
scenes.text: EMI means equated monthly instalment. A fixed payment that clears both the loan and its interest over a set time.

scenes.name: split
scenes.text: Each payment has two parts. Interest on what you still owe, and principal that reduces the loan.

scenes.name: early
scenes.text: At the start you owe the most, so most of the EMI goes to interest, and only a little cuts the loan.

scenes.name: later
scenes.text: As the loan shrinks, interest falls, and more of each payment goes to principal. It speeds up.

scenes.name: prepay
scenes.text: Paying extra early on hits the principal directly, which can save a lot of total interest.

scenes.name: rate
scenes.text: A longer tenure lowers the EMI, but you usually pay more interest overall. Check the total, not just the monthly number.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Same EMI, shifting split, interest first then principal. Follow for more on how things really work.
